items.summary: An open-source (AGPL) local MCP server: plug an iPhone into your Mac over USB and Claude Code, Codex or any MCP client can tap, type and read the screen of the real device, just like a person; it also takes orders over iMessage and Telegram, needs no jailbreak or extra hardware, and remote connections work over Tailscale. 800+ stars in five days.
items.title: Poki: Let AI agents operate a real iPhone — a local MCP server on your Mac, no jailbreak or extra hardware (released Nov 5)

items.summary: A Mac-first free desktop app whose AI teammates open real apps — Numbers, Mail, your browser — and click, type and fill things in while you watch or take over. It runs on the Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other subscriptions you already pay for, takes orders from your phone or Telegram by text or voice, runs on a schedule, and connects to 1,000+ apps including Gmail, Calendar, Slack, Notion and GitHub.
items.title: AppuBot: AI teammates that use your real apps on the Mac, driven from your phone or Telegram (Product Hunt, Nov 9)
